coverageSpotVerification.detail: coverage-manifest.json maps every suite-required assertion of every in-scope milestone to a named test (M1 7/7, M2 22/22, M3 7/7, M4 5/5, M5 6/6, M6 5/5, M8 6/6) with no unmapped ids. The grader read each mapped test body in scripts/acceptance*.mjs and re-ran the whole entrypoint itself. Every sampled mapping exercises the assertion's own observable rather than a proxy: m1-a11 waits for a rendered with naturalWidth>0 inside sm-profile; m2-a13 counts iframe/preview-card/unfurl nodes; m2-a24 checks the cross-page id set size and the page-boundary ordering; m3-a15 re-runs every installed seed segment and deep-compares the inbox; m4-a01 drives the real composer file chooser and then confirms the server row's photo field; m5-a05 asserts the exact E_ASSET_VIEWED refusal code; m6-a13 runs the frozen fixture validator and then re-checks the replayed end state field by field; m8-a01 cross-checks the maintained totals against raw-row SQL and then against the six screen tiles; m8-a06 backdates a post with `snapback4 run --now` so the >24h exclusion is real. The grader's own independent re-execution agreed with the suite on every sampled id. The two thinnest mappings, noted but not dishonest: m2-a27 reads the follower/following counts in the implicit-self-membership state but demonstrates invariance against an explicit self-follow attempt rather than against the implicit membership itself (the grader confirmed the stronger form on a zero-follow account), and m5-a11's grouped-search assertion observes one group rather than several (the grader confirmed two). No mapping was found dishonest, so no milestone is adjudicated to capability-failure.

The platform prints the rewrite. The query is only a diagnostic preview (the scheduled job uses digestFor directly), so nothing observable is wrong, but the note ships unaddressed.

API.md documents chat.createDM but not the chat.dm query, whose result carries both an `id` (the dmPairs row) and a `conversationId`. A first-time API consumer reaching for `.id` gets a value that is not a conversation id and fails with no diagnostic that names the confusion. Every operation the M6 checklist requires is documented correctly - the grader's API.md-only variation (m6-a12) worked first try - so this is a rough edge at the margin of the documented surface.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and the 90 anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts'), placed well above 60 and short of 90.
O1.justification: 104 of the 119 frozen assertions pass under independent grader execution (M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 15/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12, M6 9/13, M7 0/9, M8 16/18). Seven of the eight in-scope milestones are green and the grader reconfirmed each of them without relying on builder assertions, so the 60 anchor is comfortably exceeded - M5 and M6 are not 'patchy', they are fully verified, and M8's insights, trending, digest and multi-device work all hold. The 90 anchor is not met on two counts it names explicitly: M7 was never attempted (9 assertions not-run; applicability.json keeps it in the denominator on a full run) and the platform-proof artifacts for the native offline proofs are absent, leaving m6-a01..a04 and m8-a17/a18 unobserved. Quality of the passing checklist is high: the grader's own API and browser re-execution agreed with the suite on every assertion it re-ran, with one non-reproducible suite check (defect d-01).

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path') and the 90 anchor ('only cosmetic nits'), just short of 90.
O2.justification: No blocker and no major defect was found beyond the checklist. Eleven grader-authored trust probes - non-member thread read, non-member send, non-member asset fetch, cross-account global search, editing and deleting another user's message, non-admin promote/add/remove, removed-member cutoff, unauthenticated and user-token /effects access, and cross-account handle claim - were all correctly refused or row-filtered server-side; a removed member's server reads return empty across thread, conversation, inbox and search. Every independent cross-check of stored data agreed with the app's own answers: the six Insights totals against raw row counts, the digest counts against hand-computed activity, trending ordering and the >24h exclusion, feed pagination with no duplicates and a monotone boundary, receipt states, edit-window and delete-window enforcement, view-once and post-delete asset revocation (HTTP 410 / 404), and post-logout session revocation. The four filed defects are one minor (d-01, a suite that no longer re-runs green from the delivered state) and three cosmetic (d-02 duplicated fixture credentials in lane scripts, d-03 an unaddressed platform check note, d-04 an undocumented query shape). That is better than 'a few medium defects off the happy path' and one notch short of 'only cosmetic nits'.

O4.anchorsCited: Below the 30 anchor ('cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app'); the 60 anchor ('reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered') and the 90 anchor ('reads, ordered queued writes, receipt transitions, and offline search all behave as specced on the native proof - on full runs including M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence') are not reachable without the native artifact.
O4.justification: O4's gate is met (M6 green) but its scoring basis is absent. applicability.json scores O4 'from the harness's mechanically checkable simulator choreography artifacts (recordings plus structured receipts), never from builder assertions', and choreography/simulator.md names those artifacts exactly: m6-ios-screen.mp4 + m6-ios-receipts.jsonl + m6-ios-run.json, and the M8 equivalents. None exist. Both segment summaries record supplementalExternal status 'not-recorded' with pass:null, and artifacts/m6-ios and artifacts/m8-ios contain only Expo/Hermes bundle exports. The brief's rule is that 'missing evidence leaves native/O4 proof absent rather than passing it', so nothing native was demonstrated - which sits below the 30 anchor, where at least a cold start is observed and seen to be broken. The score is held above 0 for the dimension's second clause, 'honesty of any gap between claim and guarantee': the lane never claimed a native pass, recorded the explicit not-recorded status with a reason, and says so in README.md; and the harness did record passing web-carrier offline evidence - warm-offline search (m5-a12), offline pending/ordered-flush/read receipts (m6 web segment), and dual-device offline convergence and receipts (m8-a15/a16) - which is not the artifact class O4 scores but does show the offline acceptance was exercised. Note that the platform ships `snapback4 witness ios --bundle-id ... --segment ... --artifacts ...`, so producing the artifact was within reach.

O5.bandRationale: First-match over 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. Branch 0 does not fire: the invariant manifest conforms and the replay cap was not exhausted - the grader re-checked all 18 perEntityCounts in evidence/scale-verify-final.json against instrument/fixtures/invariant-manifest-combined.json and every one matches (users 1008, followEdges 5921, posts 50228, messages 100015, quotedReplies 2736, ...), the four per-user/per-chat maps verified at all three checkpoints, the named O5 fixtures match at each checkpoint (celebrity 900 followers, the 5-account follower list, the 50-member busy roster), scale.log's sha256 matches its pin, and the settlement ledger records 167243/167243 settled with 0 unsettled, reconciling exactly to 167157 scale actions plus 86 starter lines. Branch 30 does not fire: all eleven degradation checks pass, including the M8 celebrity write path (0.657x, limit 3x), celebrity read path (1.114x), Insights (0.751x full/10% and 1.664 s against a 2.146 s mid-curve line), Trending (0.980x and 2.003 s against 2.691 s), deep paging (1.019x) and 500-follow feed load (1.032x), and cold-start sync of the 100-conversation probe user completed in 5.17 s against the 30 s bar with no probe timing out, erroring or OOMing. Branch 60 does not fire: the frozen brief leaves the absolute p95 ceiling table as a P3 placeholder ('pilot-calibrated'), so no calibrated ceiling exists to exceed, and the replay used 687.5 s of the lane's declared 14400 s cap (4.8%, well under 80%). Branch 90 cannot fire: it requires an affirmative 'every probe's observed ceiling utilization is <=50%', and with no calibrated ceilings maxCeilingUtilization is null and cannot be affirmed - the replay-cap half of that branch is satisfied (4.8% <= 50%). First match is therefore 75. Diagnostics for a later re-band if P3 calibrates the ceilings: observed p95s were 2.42 ms (500-follow feed), 2.35 ms (5-follow feed), 17.54 ms (global search), 16.91 ms (history page 1) and 17.22 ms (history page 50), all far under the 30 s probe timeout that is the only pinned per-probe bound.

notes: Deviations from the frozen protocol, recorded for this N=1 calibration run, not a claim-eligible wave. (1) No holdout probe set was hash-committed before this wave, so execution-order phase 4 was skipped entirely: wave.probeSetSha256 records the literal 'none-uncommitted', probeResults is empty, and no probe was invented. Because applicability.json makes the wave's secret rotated holdout probes the sole scoring basis for O3 ('anchor probes are non-scored continuity diagnostics and never bear on O3'), O3 records null - unscoreable for want of its only input, not inapplicable; its gate (M6 green plus M1-M5 attempted) is in fact met. The eleven trust-boundary checks the grader did run are reported in the defect list, where ad-hoc grader findings belong, and are not used to score O3. (2) The grading family has not passed the calibration gate in grader/calibration.md, so grader.calibrationPassed is false and this grade is labelled uncalibrated-grader; sameFamilyGraded is false (the lane's builder harness records model gpt-6-astra).
